title: Global and relative cup products over an affine base
statement: Let $A\to A'$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings, $T=\operatorname{Spec}A$ and $T'=\operatorname{Spec}A'$ the affine schemes [def-pc-scheme], and $h:T'\to T$ the induced morphism. Let $p:Z\to T$ be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated morphism of algebraic spaces [def-trf-algebraic-space]: inverse images of quasi-compact spaces are quasi-compact, and the diagonal is quasi-compact. Put $Z'=Z\times_TT'$, with projections $h':Z'\to Z$ and $p':Z'\to T'$. Use module sheaves on the small etale sites [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], quasi-coherent modules [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module], module direct image and tensor pullback [def-trf-space-etale-module-functors], cohomology $H^q$ and higher direct images $R^qp_*$ computed by injective resolutions of module sheaves, and the relative and global cup products of [def-sfb-ringed-site-module-cup-product]. For quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_Z$-modules $M$ let $\theta^q_M:H^q(Z,M)\xrightarrow{\sim}\Gamma(T,R^qp_*M)$ be the canonical isomorphisms of [lem-sfb-space-affine-base-higher-image-sections], and $\theta'$ those for $p'$. Then: (i) for quasi-coherent $M,N$, integers $a,b\geq0$, $x\in H^a(Z,M)$ and $y\in H^b(Z,N)$, the element $\theta^{a+b}_{M\otimes N}(x\smile y)$ is the image of $\theta^a_M(x)\otimes\theta^b_N(y)$ under $\Gamma(T,R^ap_*M)\otimes_A\Gamma(T,R^bp_*N)\to\Gamma(T,R^ap_*M\otimes R^bp_*N)$ followed by the global sections of the relative cup product $R^ap_*M\otimes R^bp_*N\to R^{a+b}p_*(M\otimes N)$; (ii) for every quasi-coherent $M$ and $q\geq0$, $\theta'^q_{h'^*M}\circ h'^*=\Gamma(T',\beta^q_M)\circ h^*\circ\theta^q_M$, where $h'^*:H^q(Z,M)\to H^q(Z',h'^*M)$ is pullback, $h^*:\Gamma(T,R^qp_*M)\to\Gamma(T',h^*R^qp_*M)$ is pullback of sections and $\beta^q_M:h^*R^qp_*M\to R^qp'_*h'^*M$ is the canonical base-change map; (iii) the maps $\beta$ are compatible with relative cup products: $\beta^{a+b}_{M\otimes N}(h^*(u\smile v))=\beta^a_M(h^*u)\smile\beta^b_N(h^*v)$ for local sections $u,v$ of $R^ap_*M$, $R^bp_*N$, under $h'^*(M\otimes N)=h'^*M\otimes h'^*N$. No Noetherian, flatness or finiteness assumption is made on $A\to A'$, $p$, $M$ or $N$.

source.place: Tag 0FPN (lemma-compose-cup-product), applied to $Z\to T\to\mathrm{pt}$, and Tag 0H9A (lemma-base-change-cup-product) for the square $Z'\to Z$ over $T'\to T$; with spaces-cohomology.tex Tag 08EX (lemma-quasi-coherence-higher-direct-images-application) for the section isomorphisms. The combined statement is reviewer-stated.

proof.text: Work on the enlarged etale ringed sites of [lem-trf-space-enlarged-etale-ringed-site-model]. They present the same module categories, have the algebraic spaces themselves as final objects, and realize all four arrows and their composition as ringed-topos morphisms. The chart-limit normalization [lem-trf-space-chart-limit-enlarged-sections] identifies their direct images with the specified module direct images. Quasi-compactness of $p'$ follows from [lem-sfb-space-quasicompact-affine-tests]; its diagonal is a base change of the quasi-compact diagonal of $p$, so the same result makes $p'$ quasi-separated. Pullback preserves local free presentations because it is a left adjoint and sends the structure module to the structure module. Tensor two presentations by taking generators $e_j\otimes f_l$ and relations from either presentation; this again is a local free presentation. Hence $M\otimes N$, $h'^*M$, $h'^*N$ are quasi-coherent, directly from [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module]. Thus [lem-sfb-space-affine-base-higher-image-sections] applies to every theta used in the statement. The cocycle description of the Leray edge in [lem-sfb-ringed-site-leray-spectral-sequence] identifies theta with the canonical composite $H^q(Z,M)=H^qR\Gamma(T,Rp_*M)\xrightarrow{e}\Gamma(T,\mathcal H^qRp_*M)$; use the adjunction-compatible global-sections compositor of [lem-sfb-ringed-derived-monoidal-comparisons]. This also fixes theta-prime, and keeps the scalar ring $A$, respectively $A'$, even if $\Gamma(Z,\mathcal O_Z)$ is larger.

Let $s:T\to(\mathrm{pt},A)$ be global sections. The composite-counit formula and monoidality of pullback composition in [lem-sfb-ringed-derived-monoidal-comparisons] give the cup identity for $sp$: transpose either composite under $L(sp)^*\dashv R(sp)_*$. After the canonical tensor comparison, both transposes are the tensor of $\varepsilon_{p,M}Lp^*(\varepsilon_{s,Rp_*M})$ and $\varepsilon_{p,N}Lp^*(\varepsilon_{s,Rp_*N})$. These are the two counits of $sp$, so injectivity of adjunction gives $c_{sp}=Rs_*(c_p)\circ c_s$ under the compositors. Here each $c$ is precisely the tensor-of-counits map of [def-sfb-ringed-site-module-cup-product]. The global product with scalar ring $A$ factors through tensor over $\Gamma(Z,\mathcal O_Z)$: both transposes send local scalars and tensors to their products, so this is also the global product in the item. Postcompose with $R(sp)_*$ of the augmentation $M[0]\otimes^{\mathbf L}N[0]\to(M\otimes N)[0]$.

Apply [lem-sfb-ringed-hypercohomology-edge-tensor] to $K=Rp_*M[0]$ and $L=Rp_*N[0]$ on $T$. Its tensor edge equation, followed by edge naturality for $c_p$ and for the coefficient augmentation, takes the global cup identity in step 2 to the product of the two sections $e_K(x)$ and $e_L(y)$. By step 1 these are $\theta_M^a(x)$ and $\theta_N^b(y)$. By the definition of the relative product [def-sfb-ringed-site-module-cup-product], the resulting map of cohomology sheaves is $R^ap_*M\otimes R^bp_*N\to R^{a+b}p_*(M\otimes N)$. The first operation is exactly tensoring sections over $A$ and mapping to sections of their sheaf tensor. This proves (i).

Write $B_M=Rp_*M[0]$, $D_M=Rp'_*h'^*M[0]$, and let $E_M:Lh^*B_M\to D_M$ be the mate of the ringed square, followed by $Rp'_*$ of $Lh'^*M[0]\to h'^*M[0]$. The mate is [def-trf-topos-derived-base-change-map]. For clarity, the ordinary canonical base-change map in degree $q$ is $\beta_M^q=\mathcal H^q(E_M)\circ r_{h,B_M}^q$, using the scalar/cocycle map $r$ of [lem-sfb-ringed-hypercohomology-edge-pullback]. This is a map from $h^*R^qp_*M$, with no replacement of $h^*$ by an exact functor. Under the global-sections compositors, $P_{h,E_M}$ is the pullback $H^q(Z,M)\to H^q(Z',h'^*M)$: by [lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting] the square pasted with global sections has mate the global pullback unit, followed by that same coefficient augmentation. Apply the edge-pullback equation of [lem-sfb-ringed-hypercohomology-edge-pullback] with $K=B_M$, $D=D_M$, $t=E_M$. Using step 1 gives precisely $\theta'^q_{h'^*M}h'^*=\Gamma(T',\beta_M^q)h^*\theta_M^q$, proving (ii).

Before taking cohomology check the cup square for the derived exchange $\operatorname{Ex}_K:Lh^*Rp_*K\to Rp'_*Lh'^*K$. Write $\tau:Lp'^*Lh^*\cong Lh'^*Lp^*$. By [def-trf-topos-derived-base-change-map], $\varepsilon_{p',Lh'^*K}Lp'^*(\operatorname{Ex}_K)=Lh'^*(\varepsilon_{p,K})\tau_{Rp_*K}$. Transpose the two routes in the cup square under $Lp'^*\dashv Rp'_*$. Substitute this equation for $K$ and $L$, and the tensor-of-counits definition of cup. Both become the tensor $Lh'^*(\varepsilon_{p,K})\otimes Lh'^*(\varepsilon_{p,L})$ after $\tau$ and the canonical pullback tensor comparisons. Monoidality of $\tau$ follows from [lem-sfb-ringed-derived-monoidal-comparisons], since it is the composite of the two pullback compositors and the ring-compatible square identification. Hence the transposes, and so the two derived routes, agree. Naturality of tensor and of the counits allows postcomposition with the coefficient augmentations to give the same square for $E_M,E_N,E_{M\otimes N}$ and the ordinary coefficient products of [def-sfb-ringed-site-module-cup-product]. Indeed the two augmentation maps send a local tensor $(b\otimes m)\otimes(c\otimes n)$ to $bc\otimes(m\otimes n)$; the derived maps are those induced by these augmentations on K-flat models.

proof.text: Take the $(a,b)$ tensor-of-cocycles maps of [def-sfb-ringed-site-module-cup-product] in the square of step 5. The scalar maps $r$ from [lem-sfb-ringed-hypercohomology-edge-pullback] respect these pairings: locally the two routes on representatives are $1\otimes(z\otimes w)$ and $(1\otimes z)\otimes(1\otimes w)$, identified by pullback tensor comparison. A change $z\mapsto z+du$ changes the paired cycle by $d(u\otimes w)$, and $w\mapsto w+dv$ changes it by $(-1)^a d(z\otimes v)$; thus the equality descends to classes and sheafifies. Consequently the map on each factor is $\mathcal H^a(E_M)r^a=\beta_M^a$ and $\mathcal H^b(E_N)r^b=\beta_N^b$, and on the output it is $\beta_{M\otimes N}^{a+b}$. This is the equality in (iii), including all local sections by bilinearity and sheaf locality. All constructions use tensor pullback, not flat pullback; none asserts that beta is invertible. Degree zero gives the ordinary tensor-of-sections identity, and the zero module or zero ring gives zero on both routes.
